- If sentiment is strongly positive (≥ 0.67) in recent days, model tends to overestimate; reduce forecast slightly, especially after spikes.
- If sentiment is strongly negative (≤ 0.00) or volatile, model often underestimates; increase forecast to account for risk reversal or panic-driven volatility.
- After a sharp price spike, model frequently overshoots and fails to correct — apply a “cool-down” rule: reduce forecast by 1–2% for 3–5 days post-spike.
- When sentiment shows strong mean-reversion signals (e.g., alternating +/– 0.33), model often fails to adjust — align forecast with recent 7–14 day moving average.
- For 30-day horizon, model consistently underestimates true outcomes when sentiment is bullish (e.g., 2022-04-05, 2022-04-06, 2022-04-07) — apply a “bullish bias correction” by adding 1–3% to forecast if sentiment > 0.67 over last 5 days.
- If sentiment is neutral or mixed (0.33–0.67), model often fails to capture sudden volatility — use sentiment-weighted smoothing: if sentiment > 0.5, add 0.5–1% to forecast; if < 0.5, subtract 0.5–1%.
